newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - Feb 5.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - Feb 5.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

According to the first major projections for 1996/97 from the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics - the federal government's top commodity forecaster - Australia's farm sector, already reeling from chronic slumps in the beef and wool markets, looks set to suffer an even poorer performance in the financial year ahead. Page 1.

Figures released yesterday by the Bureau of Statistics revealed that retail sales dropped one percent in seasonally adjusted terms during December. This unexpected weak figure for the Christmas period has economists predicting negative GDP growth in the December quarter national accounts figures. Page 1.

Self-confessed anti-republican Prime Minister John Howard yesterday announced there would be a convention in November or December for the republic debate. The convention would be preceded by a national ballot for half the delegates. The other half of the delegates will be chosen by the federal government with quotas of young people and Aborigines. Page 2.

The federal government has embarked on a fresh bid to force the Senate to approve almost A$550 million worth of bdget cuts that were rejected last year. The Opposition, the minor parties and Independents have indicated they will vote the same way on the rejected bills as they did last year. Page 5.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Prime Minister John Howard told Parliament yesterday the government will test public feeling on an Australian republic later this year with a voluntary postal ballot to elect delegates to a constitutional convention - a move he says will provide a barometer of public sentiment on the issue which will influence whether a republic referendum is put before 2000. Page 1.

According to the latest figures from the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics - the nation's top commodities forecaster - weaker world prices will nip last year's rural recovery in the bud, with farmers facing average business losses of A$4,700 this financial year due to falling export returns in 1996/97. Page 1.

In what is regarded as the biggest Australian press event in Washington in memory, Andrew Peacock arrived in the American city yesterday to take his place as Australia's ambassador to the United States. Four television crews were there to record the long-waited occasion, including two which had flown in from Los Angeles. Page 1.

In a strong signal aimed at today's ABC board meeting, Communications Minister Richard Alston said last night the national broadcaster should soften its opposition to programme outsourcing if it wanted a A$200 million cheque for digitalisation - new broadcating technology - from the government. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Outlining the federal government's plans in Parliament yesterday, Prime Minister John Howard revealed the Coalition is relegating the constitutional debate on the republic to a lower-order political issue by announcing an historic voluntary postal vote to select delegates to its People's Convention on the republic. Page 1.

New South Wales Liberal Senator Bob Woods, who announced earlier this week he is quitting politics, has revealed Roxanne Cameron, a woman against whom he has laid a complaint with Special Branch Police for harassment of himself and his family, has applied for an apprehended violence order to be taken out against him. Page 1.

In a case which has angered New South Wales Director of Public Prosecutions Nicholas Cowdery, Zoran Udovicic, a man charged with possessing A$5 million worth of heroin, stands to be freed from Long Bay jail by the weekend because federal cuts to legal aid mean he cannot get a fair trial. Page 1.

A Bacardi-Martini Pacific advertising poster was banned in Victoria yesterday because it emitted a non-alcoholic scent of a new lemon-flavoured rum - Bacardi Limon - but it is still up in Sydney, despite concerns from New South Wales Health Minister Andre Refshauge that the campaign will affect young people and those recovering from alcohol problems. Page 3.
THE AGE

Prime Minister John Howard yesterday confirmed that a people's convention on the republican debate would take place at the end of this year. The convention will be composed of members from all states and territories for the forum, which is to debate the finer details on the Australian republic proposal. Page 1.

Despite recent successes of Australian cinema, an independent inquiry into the local film industry recommends sustained Commonwealth funding and further investment incentives if Australia is to produce further box office successes. The report also acknowldges that Australian cinema is enjoying a period of critical and commercial success which can be attributed to government support. Page 1.

A Federal Government frontbencher who resigned suddenly on Monday, Senator Bob Woods, was last night embroiled in controversy as it was revealed that an application for an apprehended violence order had been taken out on him for alleged harassment and an investigation by the Federal Police is currently under way involving allegations of impropriety into his parliamentary and travel expenses. Page A1.

According to three prominent television producers, viewers would benefit from the outside production of programmes for the Australian Broadcasting Corporation. All argued that if the recommendations of the Mansfield report into the restructurig of the national broadcaster be accepted by the ABC board today, there would be greater diversity of programming. Page A3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
